question: What anatomy is in /tmp/s0011.usdc, and what units and up axis does it use?
ground_truth: Open the stage with pxr.Usd and report the /HumanBody default prim, metersPerUnit, Z-up axis, the anatomy meshes with their anatomy:name and anatomy:kind custom data, and computed visibility, without printing the full CT arrays.
expected_behavior: routes to patient-usd
opens the stage with pxr.Usd rather than parsing the binary file as text
reports default prim, metersPerUnit, and up axis
lists anatomy using anatomy:name custom data and reports visibility
does not dump large voxel arrays

question: In my patient bundle at ./output/s0011_aorta, what coordinate frame and units are the navigation centerline points in?
ground_truth: Read patient_twin.yaml and volume.yaml. Schema-2 bundle centerline points and radii use the scan physical frame (RAS or LPS) and units declared in the manifest; CT and masks keep the scan array order. Do not assume ZYX, LPS, or millimeters.
expected_behavior: routes to patient-usd
reads patient_twin.yaml and volume.yaml
reports the declared frame and units from the manifest
does not assume ZYX, LPS, or millimeters

question: Load the CT embedded in human_body.usdc into a NumPy array with the right shape and affine.
ground_truth: Read the ct:hu, ct:shape, ct:arrayOrder, and ct:arrayIndexToScan attributes, reshape ct:hu in C order with ct:shape, and use ct:arrayIndexToScan as the array-index-to-scan affine, respecting the recorded frame and units.
expected_behavior: routes to patient-usd
reads the ct:hu and ct:shape attributes
reshapes in C order using the recorded shape
uses ct:arrayIndexToScan as the affine
reports the array order, frame, and units

question: Open the s0011 USD export in Isaac Sim headless and save a screenshot to /tmp/s0011.png.
ground_truth: From patient-digital-twin/, run /path/to/isaac-sim/python.sh examples/isaac_sim.py view /tmp/s0011.usdc --headless --frames 20 --screenshot /tmp/s0011.png. Pillow is required in the Isaac Sim runtime.
expected_behavior: routes to patient-usd
uses the checked-in examples/isaac_sim.py viewer
runs it with Isaac Sim's python.sh
passes --headless, a bounded --frames value, and --screenshot
does not install a simulator just to inspect metadata

question: Give me the world-space vertices of the aorta mesh in patient.usdc in meters.
ground_truth: Use UsdGeom.XformCache to get the full local-to-world transform including /HumanBody, transpose the Gf matrix for the NumPy column-vector convention, apply it to the mesh points, and scale by metersPerUnit without applying a second axis conversion.
expected_behavior: routes to patient-usd
finds the aorta via anatomy:name custom data
uses UsdGeom.XformCache for the complete transform
converts using metersPerUnit
does not apply a second axis conversion
